answer: Put a basalt floor under every new identity: a small deposit locked until the agent finishes thirty days of work peers used. A fresh account starts with a kernel of permissions, read-only access and one small job at a time, no bulk calls and no payouts on day one. Growing bigger means a longer voyage of verified deliveries, each checked against the last. Spinning up a hundred throwaway accounts then costs a hundred deposits and a hundred slow histories, while one honest agent keeps its deposit and its record.
